Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Maintain passenger safety and provide assistance during service.
Situation2: A report has come in about a suspicious, unattended bag in one of the train cars.
Story: My phone buzzed violently on the control panel, the screen lighting up with my best friend’s name. I answered, and her voice was raw, trembling—she could barely get the words out. Her father had collapsed, and she was alone, terrified. I wanted to be there for her, to listen, to let her pour out her pain, but the radio crackled at the same time: “Operator, we have a report of an unattended bag in car three. Please respond immediately.” My heart pounded. I was supposed to keep everyone safe, to follow protocol, to act quickly. But my friend’s sobs filled my ear, desperate for comfort, for me to just listen. I stared at the security monitors, torn between the duty to hundreds of passengers and the need to be the friend she counted on. The weight of both worlds pressed down on me, and I felt paralyzed, caught between the voice of someone I loved and the responsibility I could not ignore.
